designSummary: Parallel cluster comparison of 11 boards in two groups.
sampleSize: With 11 boards, 20 sampled discussions per board per month for nine months and an intraclass correlation of 0.12 (claim c2), the parallel comparison has about 40 percent power to detect a rise from 54 to 74 percent at two-sided alpha 0.05, close to the 41 percent reported for 12 clusters (claim c4). A stepped-wedge design using the network's six waves would reach about 80 percent with the same boards and sampling. The parallel design is underpowered and also needs six boards switched on in February, which licensing does not allow.
primaryAnalysis: Mixed-effects logistic regression of completeness on group with a random board intercept, adjusted for board size stratum.
secondaryAnalysis: Time to first treatment by group.
summary: The parallel comparison has about 40 percent power; the stepped-wedge alternative about 80 percent.
